column2: Chard stems take longer to cook than the leaves, so cook the stems first.
Serve hot with lemon and chilli flakes.
Leeks and carrots in olive oil
4 leeks (cut into 3 cm pieces)
2 tablespoons rice (washed)
1 onion
1 teaspoon sugar
Wash the leeks in plenty of water and clean the grit from between the layers.
Fry the onion in olive oil in a pot for 3 minutes, add the carrot and stir for 3 more minutes.
Add the leeks and fry for 5 minutes.
Add the rice, sugar, salt and hot water; cook covered over low heat for 25 minutes.
Add the lemon juice and turn off the heat.
Let cool to room temperature in the pot and serve.
If olive-oil dishes cool in the pot, the vegetables do not darken and keep their shape.
Serve cold with a lemon wedge.
Eggplant with green lentils
2 eggplants (diced)
Soak the eggplants in salted water for 15 minutes, drain and pat dry.
Sauté the eggplants in a pan with 2 tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat for 8 minutes until lightly golden on each side.
In a pot, fry the onion and pepper in the remaining oil for 4 minutes, add the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomato and cook for 3 minutes; add the lentils, eggplant, salt, chilli flakes and hot water.
Cook covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Serve once lukewarm.
Sautéing the eggplant first stops it from falling apart while cooking.
Serve with bulgur pilaf and yogurt.
Cauliflower with peas
1 small cauliflower (separated into florets)
1 carrot (diced)
Fry the onion in olive oil in a pot for 3 minutes.
Add the carrot and tomato paste and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the cauliflower and peas and stir for 2 minutes.
Add hot water, salt and pepper; cook covered over low heat for 18 minutes.
Remove from the heat when the cauliflower is easily pierced with a fork.
Do not overcook the cauliflower; it will fall apart and turn mushy.
Serve with yogurt and rice pilaf.
Okra in olive oil
500 g fresh okra
3 tomatoes (grated)
Trim the okra caps into a cone shape, like a pencil sharpener, without opening the inside.
Toss the okra with lemon juice and salt in a wide bowl and leave for 15 minutes, then wash and drain.
Fry the onion in olive oil in a pot for 3 minutes, add the tomato and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the okra, sugar and hot water; shake the pot instead of stirring so the okra stays whole.
Cook covered over low heat for 25 minutes.
Let cool in the pot and serve.
Soaking in lemon water reduces the okra’s sliminess.
Do not stir the okra with a spoon; shake the pot.
Serve cold or lukewarm with lemon.
Green beans with potatoes
500 g green beans (trimmed and halved)
2 potatoes (large cubes)
Trim the ends and strings off the beans and wash them.
Fry the onion in olive oil in a pot for 4 minutes, add the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute.
Add the beans and cook covered in their own juices for 10 minutes.
Add the tomato, potato, sugar, salt and hot water.
Cook covered over low heat for 25–30 minutes until the beans and potatoes are soft.
Let it cool slightly in the pot and serve.
Cooking the beans in their own juices first preserves their colour and flavour.
Serve lukewarm or cold with yogurt and bread.
Chard with borlotti beans
1 bunch chard (about 400 g)
1 cup cooked borlotti beans
Finely chop the chard stems, coarsely chop the leaves and wash.
Fry the onion and chard stems in olive oil in a pot for 5 minutes.
Add the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute, then add the rice.
Add the beans, chard leaves, salt and hot water.
Cook covered over low heat for 18 minutes until the rice is cooked.
Serve lukewarm with a squeeze of lemon.
Don’t throw away the chard stems; cook them first to add flavour to the dish.
Serve lukewarm with yogurt.
Celeriac in olive oil with orange
2 medium celeriac roots
1 small potato (diced)
Juice of 2 oranges
Peel the celeriac, slice 1.5 cm thick and keep in lemon water so it does not discolour.
Add the carrot and potato and stir for 3 minutes.
Arrange the celeriac slices in the pot; add the orange juice, water, sugar and salt.
Cook covered over low heat for 25–30 minutes until the celeriac is soft.
Let cool in the pot and serve sprinkled with dill.
Grating a little orange zest boosts the aroma.
Serve cold with dill.
Brussels sprouts with carrots
400 g Brussels sprouts (halved)
Remove the yellow outer leaves from the Brussels sprouts, wash and halve them.
Boil in salted boiling water for 5 minutes and drain; this reduces the bitterness.
Fry the onion in olive oil in a pot for 3 minutes, add the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute.
Add the carrots and sauté for 4 minutes.
Add the Brussels sprouts and hot water; cook covered for 10 minutes.
Add the salt and lemon juice and serve lukewarm.
A short blanching softens the slightly bitter taste of Brussels sprouts.
Mushroom and zucchini sauté
300 g button mushrooms (sliced)
2 zucchini (half-moons)
1 red kapia pepper
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over high heat and sauté the mushrooms for 5 minutes until the liquid evaporates.
Add the onion and pepper and stir for 3 minutes.
Add the zucchini and garlic.
Sauté for 5 minutes, keeping the zucchini firm.
Add the salt at the very end; added early, the vegetables release water.
Serve hot alongside rice or pasta.
Artichokes with peas in olive oil
6 artichoke bottoms
5 tablespoons olive oil
1 dessert spoon flour
Keep the artichoke bottoms in water with lemon and flour to stop them darkening.
Fry the onion in olive oil in a pot for 3 minutes; add the carrot, potato and peas and stir for 3 minutes.
Arrange the artichokes in the pot and divide the vegetable mixture inside and around them.
Add hot water, half the lemon juice, sugar and salt.
Cover with baking paper and cook with the lid on over low heat for 30 minutes.
Let cool in the pot and serve with the remaining lemon juice and dill.
Covering the artichokes with baking paper helps them cook evenly and keep their colour.
Serve cold with dill and lemon.
Rocket and pear salad
80 g white cheese or goat’s cheese
1 tablespoon honey
1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar
Slice the pears thinly.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes.
Whisk the olive oil, honey, vinegar and salt.
Toss the rocket, pear, walnuts and crumbled cheese with the dressing.
Slice the pear at the last moment so it does not brown.
